title: Branded types and advanced patterns interview drills

items.question: Why use branded types in TypeScript?
items.answer: Structural typing makes two string aliases interchangeable — UserId and OrderId both string. Brand adds phantom property so deleteUser(orderId) fails compile. Zero runtime cost. Factory parseUserId validates then casts — single creation point.
items.sixtySeconds: Structural swap bug. Phantom brand. Factory validates. Re-parse after JSON. C# record wrapper alternative.

items.question: Do branded types survive JSON.stringify and JSON.parse?
items.answer: No. Brands are compile-time only — wire format is plain string. After parse you must re-run factory parseUserId. as UserId at call site defeats brand. Treat boundary like unknown validation.
items.sixtySeconds: Brands erase on wire. Re-validate after parse. Factory only cast site. Class wrapper if need runtime nominal.

items.question: Implement opaque Email type with factory only creation.
items.answer: declare const EmailTag: unique symbol; export type Email = string & { [EmailTag]: true }; export function Email(raw: string): Email | null { validate regex; return as Email or null }. Consumers cannot construct without factory.
items.sixtySeconds: unique symbol tag. exported type not constructor. factory validates regex. null on fail.

items.question: When do you stop adding type-level cleverness?
items.answer: When error messages become unreadable, compile time spikes, or junior engineers cannot maintain. Prefer Zod infer for runtime+type. Brands and simple utilities yes; 50-line conditional types for one endpoint no. Module type complexity budget.
items.sixtySeconds: Readability budget. Zod for boundaries. Brands OK. Absurd conditional types no. C# generators for heavy codegen.

items.question: Compare branded string to C# record UserId(string Value).
items.answer: Brand: zero runtime allocation, compile-time only, cast escape hatch. C# record: nominal at runtime, boxing cost minimal, serialization needs custom handling. Both need validation in constructor/factory. TS for libraries in JS runtime; C# for CLR nominal safety.
items.sixtySeconds: TS phantom zero cost compile only. C# record runtime nominal. Both validate at creation. Re-parse JSON both.
